1.title: A Gift for Mom
1.topic: a boy wraps a surprise gift (a red hat) for Mom in a big box, rips the paper, fixes it with tape, and Mom loves it (family, giving, feelings)
lines: *Ben* has a *big* *box*. | It is a *gift* for *Mom*. ↘
sounds: 짧게 '이': big '빅', rip '립'. 길게 늘이지 않아요.
1.expression: Sound excited on “It is a gift for Mom,” say “Snip, snip!” quick like scissors, sound surprised on “Rip! Oh, no!”, ask “A gift for me?” with a rising voice, and end warm on “I love it!” and “Hug!”

2.title: Rest, Little Bird
2.topic: a small bird bumps into the kitchen window, a girl and her mom watch quietly without touching it until it rests, fluffs its feathers and flies away (animals, nature, kindness, patience)
sounds: bumped, rushed, looked, asked, watched, blinked, hopped, flapped
p·k·sh·ch·f 소리 뒤 -ed는 짧은 't': looked '룩트', hopped '합트'. '루키드'처럼 늘이지 않아요.
2.expression: Say “Thump!” with a sudden, loud pop, sound worried and quick on “Is it hurt?”, whisper Mom's “Shh. Let it rest” slowly and gently, read “They waited and watched” quietly with pauses, then speed up and sound joyful on “and flew away!” and “Lily cheered.”

3.title: My Very Own Library Card
3.topic: a child gets a first library card from the librarian, learns to borrow up to five books and how shelf numbers help find a topic, and picks shark books, a joke book and a dragon story (community, reading, growing up)
lines: At the *front* *desk*, | the *librarian*, Mr. *Diaz*, | *asked* me to *write* my *name*. ↘
He *printed* my *card* | and *handed* it to me. | It was *bright* *blue*! ↘
“*Now* you can *borrow* | up to *five* *books* at a *time*,” | he *said*. ↘
Mr. Diaz *showed* me | how the *numbers* on the *books* | help you *find* a *topic*. ↘
At *home*, | I *read* on the *couch* | until it was *time* for *dinner*. ↘
sounds: 입술을 앞으로 내밀고 '쉬': shelves '쉘브즈'. 's'처럼 '스'로 읽지 않아요.
입을 크게 벌려 '아'를 하고 혀를 뒤로 말아 'r': card '카r드'. '카드'처럼 r을 빼지 않게!
library, finally, write, five, time, bright
알파벳 이름처럼 '아이': five '파이브', bright '브라잇'. '이'로 짧게 읽지 않아요.
3.expression: Sound proud and excited on “my very own library card!”, read Mr. Diaz's line in a calm, friendly voice, ask “Five books?” with a surprised, happy rise, list “three shark books, one joke book, and a dragon story” with a small pause after each, and end with big excitement on “choose five more!”
practice: up to five books at a time

4.title: When Thunder Roars
4.topic: thunderstorms: ice bits in storm clouds build up electric charge, lightning is a giant spark about five times hotter than the sun's surface, the heated air booms as thunder, counting seconds between flash and boom (about five seconds per mile), and the safety rule “When thunder roars, go indoors” and waiting 30 minutes (weather, science, safety)
lines: *Crack*! | *Boom*! | A *thunderstorm* can *rattle* the *windows* | and send the *dog* under the *bed*. ↘
Inside a *storm* *cloud*, | *tiny* *bits* of *ice* | *bump* and *rub* *together* in the *wind*. ↘
It is *like* the *spark* you *feel* | when you *touch* a *doorknob* | after *walking* on a *rug*. ↘
*Lightning* is a *giant* *spark* | that *jumps* *between* *clouds* | or *down* to the *ground*. ↘
In *less* than a *second*, | it *heats* the *air* | to about *five* *times* *hotter* | than the *surface* of the *sun*! ↘
The hot *air* *pushes* *outward* so *fast* | that it makes a *loud* *boom*. | *That* *boom* is *thunder*. ↘
*Light* *travels* much *faster* than *sound*, | so we *see* the *flash* | *before* we *hear* the *rumble*. ↘
If you *count* *fewer* *seconds* *each* *time*, | the storm is getting *closer*. ↘
sounds: 혀끝을 윗니 사이로 살짝 내밀고 바람만 '쓰-': thunder. '썬더'나 '떤더'가 되지 않게!
끝의 -er은 약하게 '어r'로 혀를 말아요: faster '패스터r'. '패스터'처럼 r을 빼지 않아요.
단어를 끊지 말고 이어요: bits of ice → '빗처바이스', pushes outward → '푸쉬자웃워r드'.
4.expression: Start with a loud, sharp “Crack! Boom!”, ask “what is really happening up in those dark clouds?” with curiosity, sound amazed on “five times hotter than the surface of the sun!”, slow down and count clearly in the seconds part, read the safety rule “When thunder roars, go indoors!” strong and firm like a coach, and end bright and playful on “splash in the puddles!”
practice: five times hotter than the surface of the sun
